newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed after thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed after thin trading.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after a day of thin trading in Bogota and Medellin, brokers said.

Bogota's IBB index slipped back 0.82 percent to 862.97 on a trading volume of 1.5 billion pesos, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose a meager 0.12 percent to 13,566.49 on an uncharacteristically low volume of 1.4 billion pesos.
Medellin's main mover was supermarket chain Cadenalco, whose shares ended up 0.86 percent at 935 pesos on a volume of 486.4 million pesos.

Cement manufacturer Cementos Argos provided a second focus of interest, in an otherwise sluggish market. Its shares finished up 0.93 percent at 5,400 pesos after shares worth 291 million pesos changed hands.

"Foreign funds favored Cadenalco shares and snapped them up. There was also a deal with Cementos Argos shares, while there was no other major movement on other market leaders," one Medellin broker said. The day's session in Medellin saw shares in Banco de Colombia fall back 2.22 pesos to 440 on a trade of 4.95 million pesos and Banco Ganadero's ordinary shares sunk 0.35 pesos to 278 on a volume of 2.2 million pesos.
"The trading volumes are not at all significant, but they contributed to offsetting the effect the rise of Cadenalco and Cementos Argos had on the general index," the broker added.

Bogota's index was driven down by the 6.41 percent dent suffered by Banco de Bogota, falling to 5,615 on a volume of 6.86 million pesos and the drop in Banco Ganadero's ordinary shares, which ended down 0.71 percent at 277 on a trade of 14.1 million pesos.
"The falls were due to profit-taking by small investors who got a good return on cashing in recently purchased shares. However, the volumes are not significant," a trader said.
The Bogota exchange also saw a cross deal worth 401.3 million pesos between Cadenalco shareholders, pushing the price up 0.86 percent to 935.
